title: In the X-ray off state the main ASASSN-14ko flare stayed on the 2020-2023 clock, with an added precursor and a second peak; Las Cumbres and DECam archives, 2013-2025
abstract: Question: the repeating nuclear transient ASASSN-14ko keeps a constant 108.44-d X-ray clock in 2020-2023. Earlier studies used ASAS-SN photometry (8-arcsec pixels, whole host galaxy) and found slow, broad stall-era flares and UVW2 peaks about 5 d late in the 2022 soft X-ray off state. Are these properties of the flare or of the method, and does the off state move the flare on the clock? Data: all 923 public Las Cumbres Observatory frames (2014-2023, u' B g' V r' i') and 35 public DECam exposures (2013-2025), not used before, with Swift UVOT rates and X-ray dip times from earlier SCI work. Method: forced photometry of the nucleus after PSF homogenisation, Gaia ensemble zero points, one- and two-component flare fits (MCMC), a second-peak test, decline-only peak posteriors and refits of published clock models. Results: (1) The slow rise of flare 29 (X-ray off) is a precursor that starts 23-29 d before the clock plus a fast main rise (sigma 1.9 d, as in on-state flare 20; Delta BIC 8-32). (2) The main half-rise of flare 29 is 4.0-4.25 d after the linear clock in u' g' r' i', within 0.16 d of flare 20; the main peaks also agree. With 0.7-d rise jitter the 2020-2023 optical period is 108.44 +/- 0.11 d. (3) Off cycles 28 and 29 have a second peak 10-22 d after the main peak (Delta BIC 13-15 in UVM2, 9.5-49 in ASAS-SN g); on cycles 20-22, 30 and 31 have none. The main UV peak of off cycles is at the on-state phase; estimators that merge both peaks gave the reported late peaks. (4) UV leads optical by 0.6-0.9 d in the rise. (5) The LCO points of cycles 19 and 29 make a constant period derivative worse by Delta chi2 = 15.6 (0.5-d jitter); a three-rate clock and a sinusoid clock fit. (6) DECam shows a pre-discovery flare in 2013 December (6.8 sigma), 11 months before discovery. (7) DECam flare-37 declines need an amplitude 1.5-1.6 times the 2020-2023 median for the SPHEREx peak time; the renewed post-2023 decrease does not depend on flare 37. Conclusion: the off state added emission before and after a fixed main event and did not shift the debris clock. Limitations: one off-state flare with dense LCO data, rise only; phenomenological shapes; decline-only DECam timing depends on amplitude priors; no public data cover flare 41.

display.caption: LCO u', g', r', i' and Swift UVW2 light curves of flares 19-22 (X-ray on) and 29 (X-ray off) relative to the linear X-ray clock, divided by the model maximum. The main rise of flare 29 coincides with that of flare 20; the slow rise before it is a precursor. Dashed lines and grey bands: X-ray dips.

(a) UVW2 flares of X-ray on cycles (thin) and off cycles 28 and 29 (thick), normalised to the main peak: the main peak is at the same clock phase, and only the off cycles have a second peak 10-22 d later. (b) Main-component half-rise times of LCO and UVOT bands, and X-ray dips.

(a) Residuals of the 2007-2026 timing set from the three-rate clock with the new LCO (stars) and DECam (hexagons) points; lines show other clocks. (b) DECam i' excess of the pre-discovery flare of 2013 December with the peak posterior and clock predictions. (c) DECam r', i' decline of flare 37 in 2025 with the typical-amplitude peak posterior and the SPHEREx peak range.
